summary: ```markdown # CLO 2024.1 - Texture Mapping Function ## Introduction Hello everyone. In the version of 2024.1, we optimized the function of the sticker code, which can be achieved by directly using the hundred-point pen or unit number to enter the code. Let's learn how to enter the code through this video. ## Setting the Base Code First of all, we need to ensure that the size is changed to the base code in the object window. In this file, I will use the middle code, M, as the base code. ## Selecting the Sticker Use the editor code tool to select the heavy sticker. You can see that there is an extra part of the size in the property editor. From the menu on the right side, you can choose to use the unit number or hundred-point pen to enter the code. ### Entering Code with Unit Number If you use the unit number, you can enter the exact size of each sticker. ### Entering Code with Hundred-Point Pen If you use the hundred-point pen, you can enter the hundred-point number of each sticker. In the industry, when users enter the code for stickers, they usually use the hundred-point pen instead of numbers. This will be more appropriate for users' habit of entering the code for stickers. ## Modifying Sticker Codes Now, we are here to use the hundred-point pen to modify the hundred-point number of the S code and the L code. You need to pay attention: because the base code is M at this time, the number of M is now unable to be edited. ### Overlapping Sticker Positions If we want to overlap the position of the sticker for the code, we can do it. You can select the point that needs to be overlapped. Right-click to select the coordinates that need to be overlapped. Select X and Y to overlap here. Switch the code number to check the effect. ## Using Existing Code Information Next, let's discuss how to use the existing code information to enter the code. You can see that there is already a sticker on this board. The code information is marked with a curve. At this time, the code only involves the change of location; the size of the sticker does not change. ### Moving the Sticker First, move the sticker to one side. Then we only need to use the loop outline tool to hook this curve. After that, use the edit code tool to copy the code of a certain point in this internal shape. ### Pasting the Code Select the sticker to paste the copied code, and then move the sticker back to the original position. Finally, see the sticker code information on this board. You can observe that the code of this sticker will have a position and change in size. ## Final Steps To summarize the process: 1. Move the sticker to the side. 2. Hook this shape. 3. Switch the tool to the edit curve code. 4. Copy the four points on this internal shape. 5. Paste the copied points to the four points of the sticker. 6. Move the sticker back to the original position. The above is all the content of the sticker code in the shell. After using the new function, everyone will find it more convenient to directly input the code in the shell. ```
